explanations: record() picks a shard in 0..15 (Math.floor(Math.random() * SHARD_COUNT)), but dailyTotals reads shards 1..15 only. Shard 0 receives about 1/16 of all increments and is never summed, so impressions, clicks and spend are undercounted by roughly 6%. Pacing then lets campaigns overspend their budget. The loop should start at 0.

Write sharding distributes heavy increments for one logical counter across many partition keys, each with its own throughput. A counter item is tiny, ADD can be repeated freely, and no TTLs are used here.

UpdateCommand with ADD is applied atomically by DynamoDB on the stored value, so concurrent increments both land. There is no read-modify-write to lose updates, no condition expression, and an item key maps to one item.

The loop stops after 5 attempts, and if UnprocessedKeys is still non-empty it throws 'incomplete counter read'. It doesn't silently return partial results, doesn't loop forever, and has no GetItem fallback. (Note there is no backoff between retries.)
